scope: Only the upper-left lap-dial relocation and back-button separation were evaluated. This does not score the whole Racer UI, vehicle grounding, control panel, source art, animation, or phone usability.

source_binding.binding: for lap in range(Driving.LAPS); center = Vector2(190 + lap * 88, 68)
source_binding.meaning: Two lap-state flag dials are now centered at x=190 and x=278, leaving the back button at approximately x=66 independent and separated.

comparison_states.observed: Run03 first lap dial sat directly over the back-button area. Run04 places both dials to the right with clear visible separation; no overlap observed.
Run04 preserves clear back-button/dial separation while countdown dots remain lower and independent.
Run04 retains the repaired upper-left spacing during active play. Vehicle overlap/grounding remains visible but is outside this local review.
Both lap dials turn to completed yellow/flag state without touching the back button; the relocation holds through the payoff state.

local_acceptance.basis: Across ready, countdown, front-straight, and finish captures, the first dial no longer occupies the back-button region and the second dial remains within the upper-left HUD band.
local_acceptance.geometry_observation: Back button remains near x=66; repaired dial centers are x=190 and x=278 with radius 35, leaving visible separation from the back-button circle and each other.

remaining_open_scope: Vehicle pair remains small/overlapping and weakly grounded at front straight and bend states.
The bottom steering panel and broader UI hierarchy were not rescored here.
Animation smoothness, human control feel, child readability on M11, and device performance remain unassessed.
This local 4.8 score must not be promoted to a whole-Racer or game-wide 4.5 pass.
publication_note: Exact-byte archive path mapping; local layout score only. Other Racer visual dimensions and animation remain open.
